'''Solano''' is an [[unclassified language|unclassified]] [[extinct language]] formerly spoken in northeast [[Mexico]] and perhaps also in the neighboring [[U.S. state]] of [[Texas]]. It is a possible [[language isolate]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Campbell |first1=Lyle |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vGxQDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA194|title=Language Isolates |date=3 October 2017 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-317-61091-5 }}</ref>

==Background==
Solano is known only from a 21-word vocabulary list that appears at the end of a 1703–1708 baptism book from the [[Mission San Francisco Solano (Mexico)|San Francisco Solano Mission]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Association |first=Texas State Historical |title=San Francisco Solano Mission |website=Texas State Historical Association |date=2019-02-12 |url=https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/san-francisco-solano-mission |access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref> which hosted at least four different peoples, including the [[Xarames|Xarame]], [[Payuguan]], [[Papanac]], and [[Siaguan]].<ref name="Zamponi-2024"/> Supposedly the language is of the Indians of this mission – perhaps the [[Terocodame]] band cluster. The Solano peoples are associated with the 18th-century missions near [[Eagle Pass, Texas]].
